# SYSETUP document specifications

> Version 3.1.0 collection of 144 Markdown document authoring specifications for governance, processes, plans, technical specifications, control records, and evidence. Each specification carries standardized 5-key Semantic-Discovery YAML frontmatter and defines a document's purpose, scope boundaries, authoring inputs, finished-document contract, projections, content definitions, and quality criteria.

This collection is governed by a single project version, [3.1.0](CHANGELOG.md#310), covering all 144 specifications, [INDEX.csv](INDEX.csv), [CATALOG.json](CATALOG.json), [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md), both authoring templates, and the family registry.

The collection supports engineering, operations, security, and project documentation. Its files are authoring contracts rather than completed project documents, executable procedures, or evidence of approval or conformity.

Use progressive disclosure for discovery: (1) scan [INDEX.csv](INDEX.csv) (`family,type,title,path,summary`) to shortlist candidate paths, (2) inspect Tier-2 metadata (`topics`, `use_when`, `not_for`, `projections`) in [CATALOG.json](CATALOG.json) or inspect full 5-key YAML frontmatter (including `description`) on shortlisted candidates to confirm applicability and exclusions, and (3) read the full specification body only for confirmed matches. Each specification defines authoring inputs, unresolved-fact handling, the finished-document contract (requiring 5-key Semantic-Discovery YAML frontmatter and semantic purity on standalone Markdown outputs, plus explicit native-surface rules where applicable), content definitions, and quality criteria. Ground finished documents in authorized project facts and actual evidence; place them in their owning project's authorized documentation location.

For specification authoring and maintenance, read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) (`3.1.0`) in full. Establish reader tasks, subject boundaries, sources, exclusions, unknowns, and observable cases before classification and literal composition. [authoring/families.json](authoring/families.json) defines family responsibilities and order for validation, placement, and counts. Evaluate ordinary, incomplete, and boundary finished instances before settling literal wording, and keep [INDEX.csv](INDEX.csv), [CATALOG.json](CATALOG.json), counts, version references, and overlapping sibling specifications synchronized.

Links are relative to this repository revision so the file can accompany clones and publications on different providers. For remote retrieval, resolve them against the provider's raw-file base URL for the same revision. The specification links below are representative examples; [INDEX.csv](INDEX.csv) and [CATALOG.json](CATALOG.json) index all 144 specifications, including variants.

## Start here

- [Public overview](README.md): Purpose, directory organization, progressive-disclosure usage, and documentation scope.
- [Tier-1 CSV catalog](INDEX.csv): Compact RFC 4180 catalog (`family,type,title,path,summary`) indexing all 144 authoring specifications.
- [Tier-2 JSON catalog](CATALOG.json): Derived JSON index containing family metadata, summaries, faceted `topics`, `use_when`, `not_for`, and projection kinds for single-read filtering.
- [Specification authoring standard](CONTRIBUTING.md): Version `3.1.0` rules for 5-key Semantic-Discovery frontmatter, semantic purity, projections, deterministic composition, and catalog integration.
- [Authoritative family registry](authoring/families.json): Shared family definitions and order.
- [Structured request template](authoring/request.template.json): Version `3.1.0` mission design, source bindings, specification frontmatter, coverage, evaluated cases, representation decisions, and literal wording.
- [Specification template](authoring/specification.template.md): Leading 5-key Semantic-Discovery YAML frontmatter plus five-section spine with finished-document frontmatter, presentation, projection, role, element, and quality blocks.

## Specification families

- [Governance: internal standard](00-governance/standard--core.spec.md): Authorized mandatory criteria for a defined practice or artifact; the catalog also includes policies and an engineering guide.
- [Processes: systems engineering lifecycle](01-processes/lifecycle-process--systems-engineering.spec.md): Recurring system lifecycle coordination; the catalog also includes software and control processes, runbooks, playbooks, and work instructions.
- [Plans: systems engineering management](02-plans/semp--core.spec.md): One project's lifecycle tailoring, responsibilities, resources, and technical gates; other plans address assurance, continuity, operations, and maintenance.
- [Discovery planning](02-plans/user-research-plan--core.spec.md): Unknown user needs and contexts, recruitment, instruments, permissions, and interpretation limits.
- [Technical specifications: software requirements](03-specifications/software-requirements--core.spec.md): Traceable software obligations and verification bases; other types address needs, architecture, design, interfaces, tests, and product documentation.
- [Consumer lookup and learning](03-specifications/technical-reference--core.spec.md): Version-bound API, SDK, CLI, and configuration lookup; [tutorials](03-specifications/tutorial--core.spec.md) define supported practice progression.
- [Control records: requirements traceability matrix](04-control/requirements-traceability-matrix--core.spec.md): Directed relationships and gaps between requirements and their related sources, decisions, activities, and evidence; other types include registers, requests, and decisions.
- [Product and collaboration control](04-control/product-backlog--core.spec.md): Ordered emergent work; the catalog also defines feedback intake, review requests, debt, commercial commitments, period status, and [cumulative change history](04-control/changelog--core.spec.md).
- [Evidence: verification evidence record](05-evidence/verification-evidence--core.spec.md): Observed technical conformity for an assessed configuration; other types cover reviews, execution, validation, audits, releases, and handoffs.
- [Discovery evidence](05-evidence/user-research-findings--core.spec.md): Supported user and context findings, separate from raw elicitation sources, consumed effort, and ordinary meeting records.
